correctness.rationale: For distinct primes 5<p<q and even gap d=q-p, Q=[[1,1],[1,0]] has distinct nonzero roots mod each prime. If χ_ℓ=(5/ℓ)=+1, Q^(ℓ−1)=I; if χ_ℓ=−1, Q^(ℓ+1)=−I. The exact decompositions pq+1=(p+1)(q−1)+(2−d)=(p−1)(q+1)+(d+2), with the other factor even, give the claimed A_d or B_d residues of F_(pq+2)−1 modulo both p and q. CRT proves iff. For d=2,4 A=0 and B=4,12 with no divisor >5, so p≡2 mod5. For d≥6 both fixed Fibonacci integers are positive and p must divide one, hence p≤F_(d+3)−1. Independent modular fast-doubling and Jacobi/character checks confirmed 2046 bounded prime pairs, not used as proof of all pairs.

value.rationale: A concrete and explicit local character criterion resolves an arithmetic question for every semiprime with a given even prime gap, isolates precisely two exceptional gaps that can support unbounded prime pairs, and gives an effective finite search bound for all larger fixed gaps. It is more informative than the already-known implicit average-integrality congruence.

limitations: Only distinct p,q>5 and even d=q-p; no prime distribution or infinitude of twin/cousin primes is proved.
Finiteness of each fixed d>=6 is a bound, not a complete list of qualifying pairs.
Finite fast-doubling tests do not replace the matrix split/inert and CRT proof.
An older matrix-order/Fibonacci period identity may imply the same fixed-gap evaluation under different terminology.
No claim about existence of infinitely many prime pairs of gap 2 or 4; these are conditional iff statements.
